procedure_name: Apply for a Learners Licence
situation_trigger: Person wants to legally begin learning to drive a specific vehicle class
eligibility: Minimum age per vehicle class (16 with guardian consent for gearless <=50cc; 18 generally; 20 for transport classes)
deadline: not applicable
fee_rule: As per CMVR Rule 32 fee schedule (state smart-card charges may apply additionally)
expected_outcome: Learners Licence valid for 6 months, during which practice driving under supervision is permitted
exceptions: Guardian consent required for minors in the 16-18 gearless category
escalation_route: RTO grievance cell / State Transport Commissioner

procedure_name: Apply for a Permanent Driving Licence
situation_trigger: Learner has completed the minimum learning period and wants a full licence
eligibility: Held Learners Licence for at least 30 days (and not expired, LL valid for 6 months)
deadline: Must apply before LL expires (6 months from issue)
fee_rule: As per CMVR Rule 32 fee schedule
expected_outcome: Permanent Driving Licence issued, generally valid until age 40 for a first non-transport licence (then renewable)
exceptions: A certificate from an accredited/Government driving training school (Form 9) may substitute for the standard RTO driving test
escalation_route: RTO grievance cell / State Transport Commissioner

procedure_name: Renew an expiring or expired Driving Licence
situation_trigger: DL is nearing or has passed its expiry date
eligibility: Existing DL not expired more than 5 years (a longer lapse requires a fresh application)
deadline: Commonly cited 30-day grace period after expiry without late fee; late fee applies thereafter up to the 5-year cutoff
fee_rule: As per CMVR Rule 32 fee schedule, plus late fee if renewed after the grace period
expected_outcome: Renewed Driving Licence with updated validity
exceptions: Medical certificate (Form 1A) required for applicants above a prescribed age
escalation_route: RTO grievance cell / State Transport Commissioner

procedure_name: Obtain a Duplicate Driving Licence
situation_trigger: Original DL is lost, stolen, or damaged
eligibility: Existing DL record on file with the issuing RTO
deadline: No fixed statutory deadline; should be applied for promptly after loss
fee_rule: As per CMVR Rule 32 fee schedule
expected_outcome: Duplicate DL issued carrying the same licence number and validity as the original
escalation_route: RTO grievance cell / State Transport Commissioner

procedure_name: Apply for an International Driving Permit
situation_trigger: Licence holder plans to drive in a foreign country that recognises the IDP
eligibility: Valid Indian Driving Licence and passport
deadline: Should be applied for with adequate lead time before travel
fee_rule: As per CMVR Rule 32 fee schedule
expected_outcome: International Driving Permit issued, generally valid for 1 year
exceptions: Not all countries recognise the Indian IDP; recognition depends on the destination countrys own rules (outside MV Act scope)

procedure_name: Register a newly purchased motor vehicle
situation_trigger: Vehicle has been purchased and needs to be registered before use in a public place
eligibility: Valid sale certificate from dealer/manufacturer
deadline: Typically completed before the temporary registration lapses (commonly cited ~1 month)
fee_rule: As per CMVR Rule 81 fee schedule, plus applicable State road tax
expected_outcome: Permanent Registration Certificate (Form 23) issued
exceptions: New vehicles sold by a dealer are often pre-registered by the dealer on the owners behalf
escalation_route: RTO grievance cell / State Transport Commissioner

procedure_name: Obtain Temporary Registration for a new vehicle pending permanent RC
situation_trigger: Vehicle needs to be driven (e.g. from dealer to home/another State) before permanent RC is issued
eligibility: Valid sale certificate
deadline: Temporary registration commonly cited as valid for around 1 month
fee_rule: As per CMVR Rule 81 fee schedule
expected_outcome: Temporary Registration Certificate issued, must be converted to permanent registration before it lapses
exceptions: Not required if the dealer completes permanent registration directly

procedure_name: Renew a Registration Certificate
situation_trigger: RC is nearing or has passed its expiry/validity period (commonly relevant after 15 years for private vehicles)
eligibility: Existing RC, valid insurance, valid PUC, fitness certificate where applicable
deadline: Should be applied for before RC expiry to avoid a lapse in valid registration
fee_rule: As per CMVR Rule 81 fee schedule, plus late fee if renewed after expiry
expected_outcome: Renewed RC with updated validity period

procedure_name: Obtain a Duplicate Registration Certificate
situation_trigger: Original RC is lost, stolen, or damaged
eligibility: Existing registration record on file
deadline: No fixed statutory deadline; should be applied for promptly after loss
fee_rule: As per CMVR Rule 81 fee schedule
expected_outcome: Duplicate RC issued with the same registration number and validity

procedure_name: Transfer vehicle ownership (RC transfer) after sale/purchase
situation_trigger: Vehicle has been sold to a new owner
eligibility: Seller and buyer both identified; hypothecation (if any) cleared or financier NOC obtained
deadline: Commonly cited requirement to report transfer within 30 days of the sale (exact statutory day-count NOT_VERIFIED)
fee_rule: As per CMVR Rule 81 fee schedule
expected_outcome: New RC issued in the buyers name
exceptions: If the seller fails to file Form 29, the buyer may file Form 31 (intimation of unreported transfer) directly
escalation_route: RTO grievance cell / MACT (for disputes over liability during an unreported transfer period)

procedure_name: Change the registered address on a Registration Certificate
situation_trigger: Owner has moved to a new address
eligibility: New address proof available
deadline: Commonly cited as required within 30 days of the address change
fee_rule: As per CMVR Rule 81 fee schedule
expected_outcome: RC updated with the new address

procedure_name: Record a loan/hypothecation agreement on the RC
situation_trigger: Owner has taken a vehicle loan and the financier requires its interest recorded on the RC
eligibility: Existing RC, active loan/lease agreement
deadline: Should be completed promptly after the loan is disbursed
fee_rule: As per CMVR Rule 81 fee schedule
expected_outcome: RC endorsed showing the financiers hypothecation interest

procedure_name: Remove a loan/hypothecation entry from the RC
situation_trigger: Vehicle loan has been fully repaid or the lease/agreement has ended
eligibility: Loan closure confirmed by the financier
deadline: Should be completed promptly after loan closure
fee_rule: As per CMVR Rule 81 fee schedule
expected_outcome: RC updated to remove the financiers hypothecation entry

procedure_name: Obtain a No-Objection Certificate for interstate vehicle transfer
situation_trigger: Owner is permanently relocating the vehicle to another State/UT
eligibility: No pending challans/taxes on the vehicle
competent_authority: Regional Transport Office (Registering Authority) - originating State
deadline: Should be obtained before re-registering in the destination State
fee_rule: As per CMVR Rule 81 fee schedule
expected_outcome: NOC issued, enabling re-registration in the destination State
exceptions: BH-series registered vehicles are exempt from needing a fresh NOC/re-registration on interstate relocation

procedure_name: Assign a new registration mark after interstate relocation
situation_trigger: Vehicle has permanently moved to another State/UT and needs local re-registration
eligibility: NOC obtained from originating State (unless BH-series)
competent_authority: Regional Transport Office (Registering Authority) - destination State
deadline: Commonly cited as required within a prescribed period of relocation (exact statutory day-count NOT_VERIFIED)
fee_rule: As per CMVR Rule 81 fee schedule, plus destination State road tax (subject to adjustment for tax already paid)
expected_outcome: New registration mark assigned in the destination State
exceptions: BH-series vehicles retain their registration mark across States and do not need this procedure

procedure_name: Pay one-time or annual motor vehicle road tax
situation_trigger: Tax due at first registration, annual renewal, or interstate relocation
eligibility: Vehicle registered or being registered in the State
deadline: As per registration/renewal timeline
fee_rule: State-specific road tax slabs based on vehicle type, engine capacity, cost, and age
expected_outcome: Tax payment receipt, required for registration/renewal completion
exceptions: Non-payment can block registration renewal and may attract penalty under the relevant State Motor Vehicles Taxation Act

procedure_name: Obtain a Pollution Under Control (PUC) Certificate
situation_trigger: Vehicle needs a valid PUC certificate to comply with Section 190(2) and for use in public places
eligibility: Vehicle in operable condition for emissions testing
deadline: Commonly cited as 6-12 months validity depending on vehicle age/type (NOT_VERIFIED exact rule)
fee_rule: Nominal testing fee set by the State/testing centre
expected_outcome: PUC certificate issued, satisfying the on-road document requirement
exceptions: New vehicles commonly get an initial 1-year PUC exemption from date of first registration (commonly cited, NOT_VERIFIED)

procedure_name: Obtain an initial Fitness Certificate for a transport vehicle
situation_trigger: New transport vehicle needs a Fitness Certificate to legally operate
eligibility: Valid RC, insurance, and PUC
competent_authority: Regional Transport Office / Automated Testing Station
deadline: Should be obtained before the vehicle is first put into commercial service
fee_rule: As per CMVR Rule 81 fee schedule
expected_outcome: Fitness Certificate issued, commonly cited as valid for 2 years initially

procedure_name: Renew a Fitness Certificate for a transport vehicle
situation_trigger: Existing Fitness Certificate is nearing or has passed expiry
eligibility: Existing fitness certificate, valid RC, insurance, PUC
competent_authority: Regional Transport Office / Automated Testing Station
deadline: Should be renewed before expiry to avoid the vehicle being deemed unfit
fee_rule: As per CMVR Rule 81 fee schedule
expected_outcome: Renewed Fitness Certificate, commonly cited as valid for 1 year on renewal

procedure_name: Apply for a Goods Carriage Permit
situation_trigger: Owner wants to legally operate a transport vehicle to carry goods for hire or reward
eligibility: Valid RC, insurance, and fitness certificate for the vehicle
deadline: Permit must be obtained before commercial goods operation begins
fee_rule: As per State-specific permit fee schedule
expected_outcome: Goods Carriage Permit issued, specifying authorised routes/areas of operation
exceptions: National Permit holders may operate across multiple States under a single authorisation (subject to separate rules)

procedure_name: Apply for a Stage/Contract Carriage Permit
situation_trigger: Owner wants to legally operate a transport vehicle to carry passengers for hire or reward
eligibility: Valid RC, insurance, and fitness certificate for the vehicle
deadline: Permit must be obtained before commercial passenger operation begins
fee_rule: As per State-specific permit fee schedule
expected_outcome: Stage/Contract Carriage Permit issued, specifying authorised routes/areas of operation

procedure_name: Register a vehicle under the Bharat (BH) Series
situation_trigger: Owner is a Government employee, PSU employee, or employed by a private company with offices in 4+ States/UTs, and expects frequent interstate relocation
eligibility: Qualifying employment certificate
deadline: Available at the time of new vehicle registration (or, per some State practice, conversion of an existing RC)
fee_rule: As per BH-series-specific road tax structure (paid in 2-year instalments)
expected_outcome: BH-series registration mark assigned; vehicle does not require re-registration/NOC on interstate relocation

procedure_name: Deregister and scrap an end-of-life vehicle
situation_trigger: Owner wants to voluntarily scrap an old/unfit vehicle, potentially to claim scrappage incentives
eligibility: Original RC available for surrender
deadline: No fixed statutory deadline; voluntary process
fee_rule: RVSF-specific scrapping/processing charges (net of any scrap value/incentive)
expected_outcome: Certificate of Deposit/Scrapping issued; RC deregistered in Vahan database

procedure_name: Pay a traffic e-Challan (fine)
situation_trigger: A traffic violation has been recorded and a challan issued (camera-detected or officer-issued)
eligibility: Valid challan reference/vehicle number
competent_authority: State Traffic Police / Regional Transport Office
deadline: Commonly cited timelines for court-referral if unpaid vary by State (NOT_VERIFIED)
fee_rule: Statutory fine amount per the relevant offence in offences_penalties.csv (may be a compounded amount, not the full statutory maximum)
expected_outcome: Challan marked as paid; no further enforcement action for that specific violation
exceptions: Some challans (e.g. drunk driving, dangerous driving) are not payable online and require a court appearance

procedure_name: Contest a traffic challan in court
situation_trigger: Recipient disputes the validity of a challan and does not wish to pay/compound it
eligibility: Challan issued and not yet paid/compounded
deadline: Court filing fee (nominal, State-specific)
fee_rule: Court adjudicates the challan; may uphold, reduce, or set it aside
expected_outcome: Some serious offences (e.g. drunk driving) mandatorily require court appearance regardless of contest
exceptions: Higher court appeal (Sessions Court / High Court, as applicable)

procedure_name: File a First Information Report (FIR) after a motor accident
situation_trigger: A motor accident involving injury, death, or significant property damage has occurred
eligibility: Accident occurred within the jurisdiction of the police station
online_or_offline: ONLINE_AND_OFFLINE (e-FIR available in some States for certain accident types)
deadline: Should be reported promptly; drivers own statutory duty to report is time-bound (exact hours NOT_VERIFIED)
fee_rule: No fee for filing an FIR
expected_outcome: FIR registered, forming the evidentiary basis for insurance claims and MACT proceedings
escalation_route: Superintendent of Police (if FIR registration is refused)

procedure_name: File a compensation claim before the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal
situation_trigger: A person has suffered injury, death of a dependant, or property damage due to a motor accident
eligibility: Accident involved a motor vehicle; claimant is a victim or legal representative/dependant
online_or_offline: OFFLINE (petition filed before the Tribunal; e-filing available in some States)
deadline: No fixed limitation period under the MV Act for MACT claims (Tribunals commonly entertain delayed claims with sufficient cause)
fee_rule: No court fee for filing under Section 166 (structured Section 163A claims may follow separate fee rules, NOT_VERIFIED)
expected_outcome: Tribunal award of just compensation following the Sarla Verma/Pranay Sethi framework
exceptions: Claimant may choose the Section 163A structured-formula route instead of a full Section 166 claim (mutually exclusive per Deepal Girishbhai Soni)
escalation_route: Appeal to the jurisdictional High Court

procedure_name: Apply for compensation under the Hit and Run Compensation Scheme
situation_trigger: Victim was involved in an accident caused by an unidentified/untraced motor vehicle
eligibility: Vehicle causing the accident could not be identified/traced
competent_authority: District Claims Officer / General Insurance Council (Scheme administrator)
deadline: Commonly cited application window after the accident (exact statutory day-count NOT_VERIFIED)
fee_rule: No fee to apply
expected_outcome: Fixed compensation amount paid per the schemes benefit schedule (not the full MACT just compensation amount)
escalation_route: District Claims Officer escalation / MACT (for disputes)

procedure_name: Invoke Good Samaritan protection after rendering emergency assistance
situation_trigger: A bystander who voluntarily helped an accident victim is later questioned or asked to become a witness/involved party
eligibility: Assistance was rendered voluntarily and in good faith, without expectation of payment
deadline: No fixed procedural deadline; protection applies at the time assistance is questioned
fee_rule: No fee
expected_outcome: Bystander is not compelled to reveal identity or act as a witness unless they choose to; protected from civil/criminal liability for the assistance rendered
exceptions: Protection does not extend to acts of gross negligence unrelated to good-faith assistance (commonly cited, NOT_VERIFIED against the primary guideline text)
escalation_route: District Magistrate / Court (if protection is disputed)

procedure_name: Add a new vehicle class to an existing Driving Licence
situation_trigger: Licence holder wants to drive an additional class of vehicle not covered by their current DL (e.g. adding LMV to an existing MCWG-only licence)
eligibility: Existing valid DL in another class
deadline: not applicable
fee_rule: As per CMVR Rule 32 fee schedule
expected_outcome: DL updated to include the additional vehicle class, subject to a separate driving test for that class
